Muslims do not worship the KaꜤbah (the inviolable house in Makkah). Facing the KaꜤbah during prayer (known as the qiblah) is a matter of obedience to God's command and serves to unite the direction in which Muslims face when worshipping God across the earth. It is similar to how placing one's forehead on the ground in prostration is not worshipping the earth itself.

Worship, including prayer and all forms of devotion, belongs to God alone. Anyone who intends to worship the KaꜤbah itself would be going against the core of Islamic faith (Tawhid / Oneness of God), which teaches absolute submission and worship to God alone without partners. The KaꜤbah is a historic structure built by the prophet Ibrahim, and it serves as a historic symbol of Tawhid, which is why Muslims face it, not because it can bring benefit or harm on its own.

القرآن الكريم ليس من تأليف النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا من صنع البشر، بل هو كلام الله تعالى المنزل عليه القرآن.

2. تأخر نزول الوحي في بعض الأوقات عن النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم حين كان يُسأل عن شيء، وكان ينتظر مجيئه ولا يجيب من تلقاء نفسه.

﴿إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [الحاقة: 40]

.

The idea that Islam (submission to God) was spread by the sword is a common misconception. Historically, Islam spread through peaceful invitation (Da'wah) and convincing arguments, not through forced conversion.

While military conquests did occur, their purpose was not to force people to change their religion. Instead, these conquests allowed Muslims to travel and settle in new regions. This facilitated close contact between Muslims and the local populations. Through daily interactions, people observed the high moral character of Muslims and the justice of Sharia (Islamic law and guidance). Finding it superior to their previous ways, many chose to embrace Islam voluntarily.

Historical facts support this:
- In Mecca, the message spread purely through proof and persuasion.
- The early supporters in Medina accepted Islam solely through hearing the invitation.
- Many prominent leaders embraced Islam by choice before the conquest of Mecca.
- When the Prophet Muhammad conquered Mecca, he did not force conversion; he granted amnesty to the inhabitants, declaring them free.

Furthermore, as highlighted in the book *A Debate between Islam and Christianity*, Muslims are divinely commanded to invite others to God's path with wisdom and goodly exhortation, and to debate others—including the People of Scripture (Jews and Christians)—in the most gracious manner. Even in conflict, the Prophet instructed his commanders to first offer opponents peaceful options, such as accepting Islam or paying a tribute (Jizyah) to live under Muslim protection in peace, before resorting to fighting.

It is wonderful that you are asking this question. In Islam, differences among scholars are natural and limited to secondary, practical rulings. They do not affect the core, fundamental beliefs of the religion, which are clearly known by necessity.

These differences arise from objective, scholarly reasons when qualified scholars perform *Ijtihad* (exerting effort to find a ruling). Some of these reasons include:

*   **Access to texts:** A *Hadith* (prophetic narration) might have reached one scholar but not another.
*   **Authenticity:** Scholars may have different criteria for verifying the authenticity of a narration.
*   **Linguistic interpretation:** The Arabic language allows for different understandings. For example, in

﴿أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَاتٍ ۚ فَمَنْ كَانَ مِنْكُمْ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ ۚ وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ ۖ فَمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَهُ ۚ وَأَنْ تَصُومُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ ۖ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [البقرة: 184]
“[Observing Saum (fasts)] for a fixed number of days, but if any of you is ill or on a journey, the same number (should be made up) from other days. And as for those who can fast with difficulty, (e.g. an old man), they have (a choice either to fast or) to feed a Miskîn (poor person) (for every day). But whoever does good of his own accord, it is better for him. And that you fast is better for you if only you know.” (Quran 2:184)

, scholars differed on whether a word is implied regarding a traveler, which led to different rulings on *Fasting* while traveling.
*   **Methodology:** Different *schools of fiqh* (legal schools) may differ on whether to accept certain types of evidence, like analogy or local practices.

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) foretold that differences would occur. The great early scholars were never fanatical; they always urged people to follow the *Qur'an* and *Sunnah* over their personal opinions. As seekers of truth, we should respect valid scholarly efforts and ask God for guidance.

**Tawhid** is the core belief in Islam, and it refers to the **Oneness of God**.

Rather than just meaning that God is "one" in number, it is the deep belief that:
- **Godhood** (being the only One worthy of worship),
- **Lordship** (being the sole Creator and Controller of the universe), and
- All perfect **names and attributes**

belong to God alone.

In short, Tawhid means recognizing that God is completely unique, with no partners, equals, or associates in His divinity, His actions, or His perfect qualities.

The Arabic word **Tawhid** is translated as the **Oneness of God**.

In Islam, this is the core belief that Godhood, lordship, and all divine names and attributes belong to God alone. Rather than just meaning that God is "one" numerically, it means recognizing that He is unique and absolute in His creation, His right to be worshipped, and His perfect attributes, without any partners or equals.

In Islam, laws are established to protect human well-being and dignity. One of the primary objectives of Islamic law (Sharia) is the preservation of the human intellect.

The Qur'an explains the wisdom behind prohibiting alcohol and other intoxicants by highlighting their severe harms:

1. **Harm to the Mind:** Alcohol weakens the intellect, leading to foolishness and a loss of self-control. This often results in harmful words and actions, causing a person to lose their dignity.
2. **Social Harm:** It breeds enmity, hatred, and division among people, damaging relationships and ruining families.
3. **Spiritual Harm:** It diverts people from the remembrance of God (dhikr) and performing their prayers (Salah), which are vital for a healthy heart and spiritual well-being.
4. **Financial Harm:** It leads to wastefulness and spending wealth on what brings loss and ruin rather than benefit.

Rather than being about control, this prohibition is designed to protect our minds, relationships, wealth, and spiritual connection to our Creator.

In Islam, while the majority of scholars across different schools of jurisprudence hold the view that music and musical instruments are forbidden (حرام, which refers to what God has categorically prohibited), there are differing opinions among scholars on this matter.

Those who adopt the view of prohibition base their stance on religious texts, such as a narration recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari. Scholars explain that avoiding music has spiritual benefits, such as protecting the heart from distraction, preventing addiction to entertainment, and keeping a person focused on the remembrance of God (dhikr, which is repeating recommended phrases of praise) and prayer (salat, the prescribed ritual worship in Islam).

Because there are differing scholarly views and detailed rulings on this topic, we recommend consulting a qualified Islamic specialist or scholar for further details.

The verse you are referring to is actually

﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ [الإخلاص: 1]
“Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): "He is Allâh, (the) One.” (Quran 112:1)

, which is phrased as:

﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ [الإخلاص: 1]
“Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): "He is Allâh, (the) One.” (Quran 112:1)

This verse introduces the core concept of Islam, which is **Tawhid** (the Oneness of God). In Islam, Tawhid is not just about God being numerically "one." Rather, it is the belief that Godhood, lordship, and all of God's unique names and attributes belong to Him alone. He has no partners, equals, or associates.

As God says in another verse:

﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَنَا مُنْذِرٌ ۖ وَمَا مِنْ إِلَٰهٍ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ﴾ [ص: 65]
“Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): "I am only a warner and there is no Ilâh (God) except Allâh (none has the right to be worshipped but Allâh) the One, the Irresistible,” (Quran 38:65)

Tawhid is the greatest truth in the Islamic worldview and the very foundation of existence. It was the central message of every Messenger sent by God to humanity, as God states:

﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾ [الأنبياء: 25]
“And We did not send any Messenger before you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) but We revealed to him (saying): Lâ ilâha illa Ana [none has the right to be worshipped but I (Allâh)], so worship Me (Alone and none else)."” (Quran 21:25)

Therefore, Tawhid means recognizing God as the sole Creator and Lord, and directing all worship, obedience, and devotion to Him alone.

That is a very common question! In short, "Insha'Allah" does not mean "no." It actually translates to "If Allah wills" (or "If God wills").

When a Muslim says "Insha'Allah" regarding a future task, they are expressing their intention to do it while acknowledging that everything ultimately depends on God's will.

In the Quran, we see the importance of saying "Insha'Allah" (If Allah wills) when planning for the future

﴿وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ﴾ [القلم: 18]
“Without saying: Inshâ’ Allâh (If Allâh wills).” (Quran 68:18)

. This is because Muslims believe that all matters, including receiving help and success, happen according to God's will, as mentioned in

﴿بِنَصْرِ اللَّهِ ۚ يَنْصُرُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ [الروم: 5]
“With the help of Allâh. He helps whom He wills, and He is the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful.” (Quran 30:5)

.

So, your coworker is not trying to say "no." Rather, they are intending to complete the report while recognizing that its completion is ultimately subject to the will of God.

یہ ایک عام غلط فہمی ہے کہ مسلمان کعبہ (The KaꜤbah) کی عبادت کرتے ہیں۔ حقیقت یہ ہے کہ مسلمان کعبہ کی عبادت بالکل نہیں کرتے، بلکہ وہ صرف اور صرف ایک اللہ کی عبادت (بندگی) کرتے ہیں۔ اسلام میں تمام تر عبادات صرف اللہ ہی کے لیے ہیں، جسے توحید کہتے ہیں.

کعبہ کی طرف رخ کرنے کی حقیقت کو درج ذیل نکات سے سمجھا جا سکتا ہے:

1. **کعبہ ایک مادی عمارت ہے:** کعبہ پتھروں سے بنی ایک زمینی عمارت ہے جو بذاتِ خود نہ تو کوئی نفع پہنچا سکتی ہے اور نہ ہی نقصان پہنچا سکتی ہے.
2. **اللہ کے حکم کی اطاعت:** کعبہ کی طرف رخ کرنا اللہ تعالیٰ کے حکم کی تعمیل ہے، نہ کہ کعبہ کی عبادت۔ اللہ نے دنیا بھر کے مسلمانوں کے لیے نماز (صَلاة) میں ایک ہی سمت یعنی قبلہ (The qiblah) متعین فرمائی ہے تاکہ سب ایک رخ ہو کر عبادت کریں۔ جیسے سجدہ کرتے ہوئے زمین پر پیشانی رکھنا زمین کی عبادت نہیں ہوتا، اسی طرح کعبہ کی طرف رخ کرنا کعبہ کی عبادت نہیں ہے. قرآن مجید میں اللہ تعالیٰ کا ارشاد ہے:

﴿قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي السَّمَاءِ ۖ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَاهَا ۚ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ ۚ وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ ۗ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ ۗ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [البقرة: 144]
ہم آپ کے چہرے کو بار بار آسمان کی طرف اٹھتے ہوئے دیکھ رہے ہیں، اب ہم آپ کو اس قبلہ کی جانب متوجہ کریں گے جس سے آپ خوش ہوجائیں، آپ اپنا منھ مسجد حرام کی طرف پھیر لیں اور آپ جہاں کہیں ہوں اپنا منھ اسی طرف پھیرا کریں۔ اہل کتاب کو اس بات کے اللہ کی طرف سے برحق ہونے کا قطعی علم ہے اور اللہ تعالیٰ ان اعمال سے غافل نہیں جو یہ کرتے ہیں۔ (قرآن 2:144)

.
3. **قبلہ کی تبدیلی:** مسلمان نبی کریم ﷺ کے ساتھ پندرہ سال تک بیت المقدس کی طرف رخ کر کے نماز پڑھتے رہے، جس کے بعد قبلہ کعبہ کی طرف تبدیل کیا گیا. اس سے ثابت ہوتا ہے کہ اصل مقصد اللہ کی اطاعت ہے، نہ کہ کسی خاص عمارت کی پرستش.
4. **توحید کی تاریخی علامت:** کعبہ کو بت پرستی کی مخالفت کرنے والے اور توحید کے علمبردار حضرت ابراہیم علیہ السلام نے تعمیر کیا تھا، اس لیے یہ توحید کی ایک عظیم تاریخی علامت ہے.
5. **کعبہ کی عبادت کرنا شرک ہے:** اگر کوئی شخص نماز پڑھتے ہوئے کعبہ کی عبادت کا ارادہ کرے، تو وہ اسلامی عقیدہ کے مطابق شرک کا مرتکب ہو کر دائرہ اسلام سے خارج ہو جاتا ہے.

چنانچہ، مسلمان کعبہ کی نہیں، بلکہ کعبہ کے رب کی عبادت کرتے ہیں۔

In Islam—which means submission to God and believing in His oneness—worship includes all words and deeds that please God. Muslims only direct their worship, such as prayer, love, fear, and hope, to God alone. This is the core of Tawhid, the belief that Godhood belongs to God alone.

According to the book *Bayyinat*, facing the KaꜤbah (the cubic structure in Makkah) is not worshipping it. The KaꜤbah is merely an earthly structure of stone that cannot harm or benefit anyone by itself. Instead, it serves as the qiblah, which is the unified direction that God commanded Muslims to face during prayer to unite believers across the world. Just as placing one's forehead on the ground during prostration is not worshipping the earth, facing the KaꜤbah is not worshipping the building. In fact, early Muslims prayed towards Jerusalem for fifteen years before the direction was changed to the KaꜤbah, proving that worship has always been for God alone.

Furthermore, Muslims do not worship the Black Stone or any other creation. The KaꜤbah was built by Ibrahim (Abraham) as a historical symbol of Tawhid, rejecting idol worship. In Islamic faith, anyone who intends to worship the KaꜤbah or any stone commits shirk (associating partners with God) and goes outside the fold of Islam.

Perlu dipahami terlebih dahulu bahwa umat Islam sama sekali tidak menyembah Ka'bah. Dalam Islam—yaitu agama kepasrahan kepada Allah dengan bertauhid dan menunjukkan kepatuhan kepada-Nya—ibadah (segala hal yang diridhai Allah baik berupa perkataan maupun perbuatan, baik lahir maupun batin) hanya ditujukan kepada Allah semata. Ini adalah inti dari Tawhid, yaitu keyakinan bahwa ketuhanan, kepengaturan, serta nama dan sifat-sifat yang sempurna hanya milik Allah semata `QA:bayyinat:9`.

Berikut adalah beberapa poin penting untuk memperjelas hal ini:

1. **Hanya sebagai Arah (Qiblah):** Ka'bah adalah Qiblah, yaitu arah yang wajib dihadap ketika umat Islam mendirikan shalat (ibadah tertentu yang dimulai dengan takbir dan diakhiri dengan salam) `QA:bayyinat:9:2`. Menghadap ke arah Ka'bah adalah bentuk ketaatan kepada perintah Allah untuk menyatukan arah umat Islam di seluruh dunia saat beribadah, bukan menyembah bangunan itu sendiri. Sama halnya ketika bersujud, umat Islam meletakkan dahi di atas tanah, namun mereka tidak sedang menyembah tanah `QA:bayyinat:9:2`.

2. **Benda Mati yang Tidak Memberi Manfaat atau Mudarat:** Ka'bah adalah bangunan bumi dari batu yang tidak dapat mendatangkan manfaat maupun mudarat dengan sendirinya `QA:bayyinat:9:2`. Allah berfirman bahwa Dia menjadikan Ka'bah, Baitullah yang suci, sebagai penopang (urusan kehidupan, keamanan, dan manfaat) bagi manusia

﴿۞ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ الْكَعْبَةَ الْبَيْتَ الْحَرَامَ قِيَامًا لِلنَّاسِ وَالشَّهْرَ الْحَرَامَ وَالْهَدْيَ وَالْقَلَائِدَ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِتَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [المائدة: 97]
“Allâh has made the Ka‘bah, the Sacred House, an asylum of security and benefits (e.g.Hajj and ‘Umrah) for mankind, and also the Sacred Month and the animals of offerings and the garlanded (people or animals marked with the garlands on their necks made from the outer part of the stem of the Makkah trees for their security), that you may know that Allâh has knowledge of all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth, and that Allâh is the All-Knower of each and everything.” (QS 5:97)

.

3. **Perubahan Arah Kiblat secara Sejarah:** Sebagai bukti bahwa ibadah ditujukan hanya kepada Allah dan bukan kepada bangunannya, umat Islam sempat mendirikan shalat dengan menghadap ke Baitul Maqdis selama lima belas tahun sebelum akhirnya arah Qiblah diubah ke Ka'bah `QA:bayyinat:9:2`.

4. **Simbol Sejarah Tawhid:** Ka'bah memiliki hubungan sejarah yang erat dengan Tawhid karena dibangun oleh Nabi Ibrahim, pemimpin orang-orang yang lurus (Al-Hunafa'). Dengan pembangunannya tersebut, beliau membatalkan penyembahan berhala, sehingga Ka'bah menjadi simbol sejarah bagi Tawhid `QA:bayyinat:9`.

5. **Niat dalam Beribadah:** Di dalam akidah Islam (keyakinan kokoh dalam Islam), siapa pun yang berniat menyembah Ka'bah ketika menghadap kepadanya dalam shalat, maka ia telah berbuat syirik (menyekutukan Allah), menjadikan Ka'bah sebagai tuhan selain Allah, dan keluar dari lingkaran akidah Islam `QA:bayyinat:9:2`.

Semoga penjelasan ini membantu Anda memahami bahwa umat Islam hanya menyembah Allah Yang Maha Esa, dan Ka'bah hanyalah arah pemersatu dalam ibadah kami.

It is a common question, but when we look closely at the historical facts and the text of the Qur'an itself, we find clear reasons why the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ could not have written it:

1. **The Delay of Revelation (the process of God sending His guidance):** There were times when the Prophet ﷺ was asked difficult questions by skeptics or faced painful situations (such as the false rumors spread about his family). He would wait for days or weeks, refraining from answering until he received Revelation. If he were the author, he would not have left himself in suspense or distress; he would have simply made up an answer immediately.
2. **Self-Admonishment:** The Qur'an contains verses where God gently admonishes the Prophet ﷺ. A person writing a book to claim prophethood would not include corrections or criticisms of himself.
3. **Unmatched Knowledge and Miracles:** The Qur'an contains historical, scientific, rhetorical, and legislative details that no human in 7th-century Arabia could have known, and it challenges humanity to produce even a single chapter like it.
4. **His Character:** Before his prophethood, he was universally known among his people as the "Truthful and Trustworthy." It is illogical that someone who never lied to people would suddenly start lying about God.

The Qur'an itself addresses its divine origin, as mentioned in

﴿إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [الحاقة: 40]
“That this is verily, the word of an honoured Messenger [i.e. Jibrîl (Gabriel) or Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم which he has brought from Allâh].” (Quran 69:40)

.

* **وحی کا انتظار:** کئی بار جب لوگوں نے آپ صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم سے سوالات پوچھے، تو آپ نے جواب دینے کے لیے وحی کا انتظار کیا (جیسے واقعہ افک میں وحی کا انتظار کرنا)۔ اگر یہ آپ کی اپنی تصنیف ہوتی تو آپ کو انتظار کرنے کی ضرورت نہ پڑتی۔
* **عتاب (نصیحت) کی آیات:** قرآن میں کچھ مقامات پر اللہ تعالیٰ نے نبی کریم صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم کو نرمی سے ٹوکا یا نصیحت فرمائی ہے۔ کوئی بھی انسان خود ایسی کتاب نہیں لکھے گا جس میں اس کی اپنی اصلاح یا عتاب کا ذکر ہو۔
* **غیب کی خبریں اور معجزات:** قرآن میں ماضی اور مستقبل کی ایسی غیب (unseen) کی باتیں اور علمی و تاریخی حقائق موجود ہیں جو اس دور کے کسی انسان کے لیے جاننا ناممکن تھا۔
* **آپ کا کردار:** آپ صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم اپنی پوری زندگی میں "صادق اور امین" (سچے اور امانت دار) مشہور تھے۔ جس انسان نے کبھی انسانوں سے جھوٹ نہ بولا ہو، وہ اللہ پر جھوٹ کیسے باندھ سکتا ہے؟

الحقيقة التاريخية والشرعية هي أن الإسلام لم ينتشر بحد السيف، بل انتشر بالدعوة (وهي التعريف بالإسلام والدعوة إليه بالحكمة) والحجة الواضحة، فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يُكره أحداً على الدخول في الدين.

ويمكننا فهم ذلك من خلال عدة جوانب:
أولاً: انتشر الإسلام في مناطق واسعة جداً لم تدخلها جيوش المسلمين قط، مثل الصين، وإندونيسيا (جاوة وسومطرة)، وأجزاء واسعة من إفريقيا، وذلك عن طريق التجار والمهاجرين الذين تميزوا بالأخلاق والأمانة.

ثانياً: في البلاد التي فُتحت، لم يكن الهدف إجبار الناس على اعتناق الدين، بل كان الفتح يمهد لتعايش المسلمين مع أهل البلاد. وعندما احتك الناس بالمسلمين ورأوا عدالة الشريعة (وهي أحكام الدين وتشريعاته الحكيمة) وسمو أخلاقهم، دخلوا في الإسلام طواعية.

ثالثاً: حتى عندما هُزم المسلمون عسكرياً أمام المغول، استطاع دعاتهم جذب هؤلاء الفاتحين أنفسهم لاعتناق الإسلام بفضل قوة هذا الدين وإقناعه.

فالمنهج الأساسي في الإسلام هو دعوة الناس بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة (وهي التذكير المقرون بالترغيب والترهيب المؤثر في النفوس)، ومجادلة الجميع -بمن فيهم أهل الكتاب (وهم اليهود والنصارى)- بالتي هي أحسن.

(انظر: كتاب "بينات: أسئلة وأجوبة عن الإسلام"، وكتاب "مناظرة بين الإسلام والنصرانية").

It is a common misunderstanding to take passages from the Qur'an out of their context. The verses concerning fighting do not command Muslims to kill anyone they find. Rather, they apply specifically to active combatants and aggressors who initiated hostility against the Muslim community.

In Islam (submitting to God in oneness and obeying Him), the preservation of human life is a fundamental objective. Fighting, or Jihad (striving to defend against aggressors and uphold justice), is only legislated for self-defense, repelling oppression, and establishing peace. It is never meant for shedding innocent blood or forcing people to convert.

Islamic guidance establishes strict ethical rules for warfare:
- It is strictly forbidden to kill those who cannot fight, such as women, children, the elderly, and monks.
- Harming prisoners of war, mutilation, and treachery are completely prohibited.
- The Prophet's way, or Sunnah, emphasizes preferring peace and safety over conflict.

Furthermore, the Qur'an promotes high moral character and peaceful disengagement from hostility, as shown in

﴿وَإِذَا سَمِعُوا اللَّغْوَ أَعْرَضُوا عَنْهُ وَقَالُوا لَنَا أَعْمَالُنَا وَلَكُمْ أَعْمَالُكُمْ سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ لَا نَبْتَغِي الْجَاهِلِينَ﴾ [القصص: 55]
“And when they hear Al-Laghw (dirty, false, evil vain talk), they withdraw from it and say: "To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be to you. We seek not (the way of) the ignorant."” (Quran 28:55)

. While fighting is a grave matter, the Qur'an explains that persecuting people, expelling them from their homes, and preventing them from practicing their faith is far worse

﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الشَّهْرِ الْحَرَامِ قِتَالٍ فِيهِ ۖ قُلْ قِتَالٌ فِيهِ كَبِيرٌ ۖ وَصَدٌّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ وَالْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَإِخْرَاجُ أَهْلِهِ مِنْهُ أَكْبَرُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ ۚ وَالْفِتْنَةُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ ۗ وَلَا يَزَالُونَ يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَنْ دِينِكُمْ إِنِ اسْتَطَاعُوا ۚ وَمَنْ يَرْتَدِدْ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ فَيَمُتْ وَهُوَ كَافِرٌ فَأُولَٰئِكَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ ۖ وَأُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾ [البقرة: 217]
“They ask you concerning fighting in the Sacred Months (i.e. 1st, 7th, 11th and 12th months of the Islâmic calendar). Say "Fighting therein is a great (transgression) but a greater (transgression) with Allâh is to prevent mankind from following the Way of Allâh, to disbelieve in Him, to prevent access to Al-Masjid-Al-Harâm (at Makkah), and to drive out its inhabitants, and Al-Fitnah is worse than killing. And they will never cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion (Islâmic Monotheism) if they can. And whosoever of you turns back from his religion and dies as a disbeliever, then his deeds will be lost in this life and in the Hereafter, and they will be the dwellers of the Fire. They will abide therein forever."” (Quran 2:217)

Historically, the battles during the Prophet's era were highly disciplined, resulting in a total of only 1,018 casualties on both sides. This stands in sharp contrast to other historical conflicts, such as the Crusader massacre of around sixty thousand civilians in Jerusalem.

Islam is defined by its sacred texts and the teachings of its scholars, not by the selective actions of individuals.

1۔ **دلیل کا نہ پہنچنا:** بعض اوقات ایک مجتہد تک کوئی خاص Hadith (حدیث) نہیں پہنچ پاتی، اس لیے وہ اپنے علم کے مطابق فیصلہ کرتا ہے، جبکہ دوسرے عالم تک وہ پہنچ جاتی ہے۔
2۔ **Hadith کی صحت کا معیار:** کسی حدیث کی صحت کو پرکھنے کے لیے علماء کے شرائط مختلف ہو سکتے ہیں، جس کی وجہ سے ایک عالم اسے قبول کرتا ہے اور دوسرا اس کی سند پر جرح کرتا ہے۔
3۔ **دلائل کا بظاہر ٹکراؤ:** بعض اوقات مختلف احادیث میں بظاہر تعارض نظر آتا ہے، جس کو حل کرنے میں علماء کا فہم مختلف ہو سکتا ہے۔
4۔ **اصولی قواعد کا اختلاف:** مختلف فقہی مذاہب (Schools of fiqh) کے نزدیک بعض دلائل کی حجیت (جیسے قیاس یا اہل مدینہ کا عمل) میں اختلاف ہوتا ہے۔
5۔ **قرآن کی مختلف قرأتیں:** قرآن مجید کی مختلف قرأتوں کی وجہ سے بھی فہم اور استنباط میں فرق آ سکتا ہے۔

یہ تمام اختلافات علمی Ijtihad (اجتہاد) کا نتیجہ ہیں، نہ کہ ذاتی خواہشات یا دنیاوی فائدے کا۔ ائمہ کرام نے ہمیشہ تاکید کی کہ اگر ان کا کوئی قول قرآن یا سنت کے خلاف ہو تو اسے چھوڑ دیا جائے۔

The correct term for الشريعة is "Sharia" or Islamic law and guidance.

It is not just criminal law. Rather, it refers to the total sum of rules and regulations that God has set for His servants and revealed to His Messenger, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). This includes detailed rulings covering many aspects of life, such as belief, worship, transactions, and morality Sharia / Islamic law and guidance.

In Islam, which is the submission to God through faith and obedience, the prohibition of pork is clearly stated in the Quran

﴿قُلْ لَا أَجِدُ فِي مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّمًا عَلَىٰ طَاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً أَوْ دَمًا مَسْفُوحًا أَوْ لَحْمَ خِنْزِيرٍ فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ أَوْ فِسْقًا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ ۚ فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلَا عَادٍ فَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [الأنعام: 145]
“Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): "I find not in that which has been revealed to me anything forbidden to be eaten by one who wishes to eat it, unless it be Maitah (a dead animal) or blood poured forth (by slaughtering or the like), or the flesh of swine (pork); for that surely is impure or impious (unlawful) meat (of an animal) which is slaughtered as a sacrifice for others than Allâh (or has been slaughtered for idols, or on which Allâh’s Name has not been mentioned while slaughtering). But whosoever is forced by necessity without wilful disobedience, nor transgressing due limits; (for him) certainly, your Lord is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful."” (Quran 6:145)

.

Scholars and researchers have discussed various aspects of the wisdom behind this ruling. From a health and medical perspective, some point out that pork can carry harmful germs and a high level of uric acid, which can lead to various health issues. Others mention that what we consume can influence our physical and spiritual well-being, and the pig is described as having undesirable traits.

However, a fundamental principle is that God—out of His mercy and wisdom—protects humanity through what He permits (Permissible) and forbids (Forbidden). Ultimately, following God's guidance is an act of obedience and trust in His wisdom, much like how human understanding of certain medical or physical benefits can develop over time.

أهلاً بك. ليس الهدف من الأحكام منع الجمال، بل حرص الشريعة (وهي الأحكام والهدي المنظم لحياة الإنسان) على مصلحته وحمايته. ومن أعظم مقاصد الشريعة حفظ العقل، ولذلك جاء تحريم الخمر والميسر لما تسببه من مفاسد عظيمة؛ فهي تُضعف عقل شاربها وتوقع العداوة والبغضاء بين الناس، وتصُدُّ عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة الصلاة. كما أنها تُؤدي إلى إنفاق الأموال بلا فائدة وتسبب الخسران وإفساد البيوت، فجاء التحريم حمايةً للإنسان والمجتمع من هذه الأضرار.
